docs.title: Buy Atul Ltd For Target Rs.7,100 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
Weakness in life science chemicals offsets growth of performance chemicals 
* Atul (ATLP) reported a weak performance in 2QFY27, as EBITDA declined 8% YoY to INR2.5b, led by a 35% EBIT decline in the Life Science Chemicals segment, which was primarily offset by 23% EBIT growth in the Performance & Other Chemicals segment.
* We reduce our FY27/FY28 earnings estimates by 6% each to factor in the weaker-than-expected operating performance.
* The stock trades at ~20.4x/18x FY27E/FY28E EPS of INR272.2/INR309.9 and ~13.2x/11.5x FY27E/FY28E EV/EBITDA. We value the stock at 23x FY28E EPS to arrive at our TP of INR7,100. Reiterate BUY.
 Weak operating performance due to the Life Science Chemicals business 
* ATLP’s revenue grew 21% YoY to INR18.7b, led by 31% revenue growth in Performance Chemicals to INR15b, while Life Science Chemicals’ revenue declined 3% YoY to INR4.3b.
* Gross margin stood at 40.3% (vs. 46.6% in 2QFY26), and EBITDA margin contracted 410bp YoY to 13.1% (est. 16.8%).
* Consolidated EBITDA declined 8% YoY to ~INR2.5b (vs. our est. of INR3b.), and adj. PAT declined by 13% YoY to INR1.6b (est. INR1.9b).
* Life Science Chemicals’ EBIT margin stood at 16.3% (down 660bp YoY), while EBIT stood at INR697m. Performance Chemicals' EBIT margin stood at 8.5% (down 60bp YoY), and EBIT came in at INR1.3b.
* For 1HFY27, ATLP’s revenue/EBITDA/Adj PAT grew 23%/27%/31% to INR37.2b/INR6.4b/INR4.1b.
* Gross debt stood at INR1.7b vs INR1.8b as of Mar’26. CFO stood at INR3.9b against INR5.1b as of Sep’25.
* The Board declared buy-back of shares for an amount not exceeding INR900m, at a maximum price of INR7,500 per equity share.
* We expect ATLP to regain its healthy momentum, led by:
1) capacity expansion for its key products in aromatics and bulk chemicals
2) new projects and unrealized revenue potential from existing capacities
3) debottlenecking in existing capacities across all major segments
4) entry into value-added products in chemical intermediates
5) launch of in-house developed novel products in the crop protection segment
6) expansion of market reach to new geographies.
* The stock trades at ~20.4x/18x FY27E/FY28E EPS of INR272.2/INR309.9 and ~13.2x/11.5x FY27E/FY28E EV/EBITDA. We value the stock at 23x FY28E EPS to arrive at our TP of INR7,100. Reiterate BUY.

docs.title: Kotak Mahindra Bank shares in focus on Mon Oct 26 after Q2 results 2026: Should you buy, sell or hold? Experts weigh in
docs.text:
On a standalone basis, the bank's profit after tax increased 29% to ₹ 4,212 crore, supported by growth in core income and lower provisions. Net interest income (NII), the difference between interest earned and interest expended, grew 16% year-on-year to ₹ 8,459 crore. However, net interest margin (NIM) contracted by 0.23 percentage points during the quarter, partly due to the bank's mobilisation of ₹ 55,344 crore in FCNR(B) deposits under the Reserve Bank of India's concessional swap facility. The bank also disbursed loans worth ₹ 16,110 crore under the FCNR(B) scheme, which permitted leveraged borrowing against deposits. Kotak Mahindra Bank share price on Friday, 23 October ended 1.70% lower at ₹ 430.10 apiece on the BSE. Managing Director and CEO Ashok Vaswani said the bank expects to maintain its net interest margins during the remaining quarters of the financial year. However, the deployment of funds raised through the FCNR(B) facility could continue to weigh on margins in the coming quarters, as the money has not yet been fully utilised. Vaswani said the impact could be partly offset by RBI rate hikes, given that around 60% of the bank's loan book is linked to the repo rate. During the September quarter, Kotak Mahindra Bank used FCNR(B) funds to reduce its high-cost borrowings through Inter-Bank Participation Certificates (IBPCs). It also acquired certain loans from its wholly owned subsidiary, Kotak Mahindra Investments. The bank said that excluding the impact of the FCNR(B)-related transactions, loan growth would have been 19%, while deposit growth would have stood at 13%. Investors will now assess whether strong earnings growth and advances can sustain the bank's performance, while monitoring the trajectory of net interest margins and the impact of deploying FCNR(B) funds in the coming quarters. Nuvama Institutional Equities said Kotak Mahindra Bank’s credit growth accelerated to 25% year-on-year, or 19% excluding FCNR(B)-related lending and the Kotak Mahindra Investments portfolio. However, funding costs associated with FCNR(B) deposits led to a 22-basis-point quarter-on-quarter decline in net interest margin (NIM) to 4.3%. Along with higher provisions for standard assets, this resulted in a largely in-line profit after tax (PAT) of ₹ 4,200 crore, with return on assets (RoA) at 1.9%. The brokerage expects the deployment of FCNR(B) deposits towards lending, along with the interest-rate hike cycle, to help the bank recover its margins over the next two to three quarters. It believes sustained credit growth and an improvement in RoA and return on equity (RoE) to 2–2.1% and 12–15%, respectively, under the new management could support a re-rating of the stock. Nuvama has retained its 'Buy' rating with a target price of ₹ 550 per share. Systematix Institutional Equities said Kotak Mahindra Bank reported a standalone PAT of ₹ 4,210 crore in Q2 FY27, up 29.5% year-on-year and 2.2% sequentially. The result was marginally below its estimate but 2% above Bloomberg consensus, supported by higher net interest income and continued cost discipline. The bank’s NIM stood at 4.31%, down 22 basis points quarter-on-quarter and 23 basis points year-on-year, largely due to FCNR(B) deposit mobilisation and related advances. Systematix has revised its estimates to account for strong advances growth and further margin movements, while introducing FY29 estimates. The brokerage has maintained its 'Buy' rating and raised its target price to ₹ 510 from ₹ 475. It values the standalone bank at 2 times its estimated FY28 adjusted book value per share of ₹ 173 and assigns ₹ 161 per share to its subsidiaries and associates. docs.title: Buy Godrej Properties Ltd For Target Rs.2,200 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
Strong launch pipeline to support 2HFY27 performance BD continues in 2Q; launch pipeline remains healthy 
Godrej Properties (GPL) added one new project in Marine Lines, MMR, offering a GDV potential of INR60b. Overall, in 1HFY27, it added INR155b GDV, including INR90b from group housing projects in NCR and INR5b of plotted development in Chennai, apart from the addition in 2Q. With these projects, GPL has already achieved 78% of its annual BD guidance of INR200b. It launched new projects with INR55b GDV in 2QFY27 (INR160b in 1H), and the planned pipeline of INR320b launches in 2H would fuel pre-sales growth in the coming quarters.
 Sustenance sales drives in-line 2Q; we maintain our estimates 
In 2QFY27, pre-sales declined 6% YoY to INR80b, but were in line. Since some of the launches slipped to 3QFY27, the 2Q performance was driven by sustenance sales, which contributed 63% of the quarterly bookings. Regionally, NCR and MMR drove the 2Q bookings, each accounting for a 24% share and together contributing INR38.3b to the quarterly pre-sales. These were followed by Bengaluru (INR15.6b; 20% share), Pune (INR9.8b; 12%) and Hyderabad (INR7.8b; 10%). Other regions contributed to 11% of pre-sales (INR8.6b). Given the healthy launch pipeline and sustenance inventory, GPL remains confident of meeting its INR390b pre-sales guidance in FY27 (+14% YoY). We maintain our expectation of a 10% CAGR in pre-sales to INR413b during FY26-28E.
 Targets INR200-210b of cumulative NOCF in FY27-28 
Collections rose 31% YoY to INR53b, 16% higher than our estimate, while operating cash flow stood at INR15.8b during the quarter. The company has guided cumulative collections of ~INR547b and INR200-210b of OCF over FY27- 28, of which it has already collected INR96.7b. This collection translated into an OCF of INR19.8 as of 1HFY27. Based on the pre-sales growth and progress in execution, we expect collections to post a 17% CAGR, reaching INR274b during FY26-28E. Net debt rose INR2.7b QoQ to INR79b in 2Q, while net D/E remained comfortable at 0.41x. We expect net debt of INR84b/INR75b in FY27/FY28.
In 2QFY27, GPL’s revenue surged 161% YoY to INR19.4b. Operating loss stood at INR4.7b. PAT declined 64% YoY to INR1.5b. Management has guided a 20% RoE in FY28. As of 1HFY27, the company’s revenue grew 108% YoY to INR24.4b. Operating loss remained flat YoY at INR7.6b. PAT declined 51% YoY to INR4.9b.
* GPL delivered in-line pre-sales on the back of strong sustenance sales and benefits of diversification across many regions. Further, collections growth has been healthy, which is encouraging. The continuing BD activity as well as launches planned in the coming quarters provide comfortable growth visibility over the medium term. While net debt increased in 2QFY27 due to the project additions, leverage remains at comfortable levels
* We like the company’s intense focus on generating better FCF in the coming quarters, and the profitability profile is likely to improve over the medium term.
* We retain the 15% NAV premium on the residential business. However, since we have increased the WACC rate to 11.1% (from 10.6% earlier) and widened the cap rate on commercial to 8.5% (from 8.0% earlier), our TP has been reduced to INR2,200. Reiterate BUY.

docs.title: Buy Jindal Stainless Ltd For Target Rs.910 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
Strong NSR and volume recovery drive earnings Outlook positive as new capacity ramps up 
* Jindal Stainless (JDSL) posted in-line revenue of INR129b (+18% YoY/+14% QoQ) in 2QFY27. The growth was led by strong ASP and volume recovery following the gas supply disruption that muted volumes in 1Q.
* Reported EBITDA was INR14.3b, which came largely in-line with our estimate of INR15b, registering 3% YoY and 8% QoQ growth. This was mainly driven by better volume and NSR, while partially offset by higher RM cost during the quarter. ? APAT for the quarter stood in line at INR8.1b, up 2% YoY and 5% QoQ.
* For 1HFY27, revenue stood at INR242b (+15% YoY) and EBITDA at INR28b (+2% YoY), whereas APAT came in at INR16b (+5% YoY).
* Sales volume for the quarter came in line at 664kt, up 3% YoY and 14% QoQ, marking a resilient recovery following the operational disruptions in 1Q. The disruptions were led by geopolitical challenges and industrial gas availability constraints. ? ASP stood at INR1,93,773/t, up 15% YoY and flat QoQ, fueled by sustenance of SS prices during the quarter.
* Export share remained flat QoQ to 11% during the quarter, as JSL continued to diversify its global reach toward South Korea, Colombia, South Africa, Brazil, and Japan.
* EBITDA/t at INR21,568 (vs. our estimate of INR22,650/t) stood flat YoY, while it declined 6% QoQ due to RM costs inflation during the quarter.
* The consolidated net debt remained steady at ~INR31b, translating to net debt/EBITDA of 0.55x as of 2QFY27.
 Highlights from the management commentary 
* Management revised its FY27 volume growth guidance to 4-6% from the earlier 7-9%, primarily reflecting the impact of Q1 disruptions and volatile geopolitical developments. However, EBITDA/t guidance was increased to INR20,000-22,000 from INR18,000-20,000, supported by higher focus on value-added products and product mix optimization.
* Management expects a strong recovery in volumes during 2HFY27, supported by the normalization of operations, gradual ramp-up of downstream facilities, and healthy demand across key end-use segments.
* Management reiterated 3.5mtpa sales volume target for FY29, with all expansion projects and capex plans remaining intact. The long-term growth trajectory remains unaffected by near-term operational disruptions.
* Industrial gas availability remained stable during 2QFY27, with no recurrence of disruptions during the quarter. The transition to natural gas has strengthened operational resilience, although the company remains watchful of geopolitical developments and potential energy price volatility
* JDSL continued to report strong earnings in 2QFY27, supported by volume recovery and sustained NSR, partially offset by RM cost escalation during the quarter. Going forward, we expect earnings to remain strong in FY27/28, mainly on account of incremental volumes from newly added capacity and healthy SS prices offsetting nickel prices volatility.
* At the industry level, SS demand is set for strong growth and is projected to reach +7mt by FY31, driven by domestic SS consumption. As the dominant player in SS space, we believe JDSL is well-placed to capitalize on this robust demand outlook, with higher VAP supporting margins.
* We maintain our earnings estimates for FY27/28 with EBITDA projected to range between INR21,000-22,000/t. JDSL has maintained a resilient B/S, with consol. net debt/EBITDA at 0.55x as of 2QFY27, which is likely to allow it to divert future cash flow toward the next leg of expansion.
* At CMP, the stock trades at 8.3x EV/EBITDA on FY28 estimates. We reiterate our BUY rating with a TP of INR910 (premised on 11x EV/EBITDA on FY28E).

docs.title: Buy Shriram Finance Ltd For Target Rs.1,155 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
Mixed quarter; caution on asset quality clouds near-term outlook Weak monsoonslead to higher slippages & writeoffs; credit cost guidance raised 
* Shriram Finance (SHFL)’s 2QFY27 PAT rose ~60% YoY to ~INR36.8b (in line). NII in 2QFY27 grew ~40% YoY to INR84.1b (in line). Other income grew ~15% YoY to INR4.2b (~8% lower than our est.).
* Opex grew ~4% YoY to INR20.2b (~9% lower than MOFSLe). The cost-toincome ratio dipped ~290bp QoQ to ~22.9% (PQ: 25.9%/PY: 30.5%). SHFL expects its C/I ratio to remain at ~25% and Opex/AUM at ~2.5% over the medium to long term. We model the C/I ratio at 24-25% over FY27-28.
* PPoP grew 53% YoY to ~INR68.1b (~7% beat). Credit costs stood at ~INR18.8b (~20% higher than MOFSLe) translating into annualized credit costs of ~2.35% (PQ and PY: 1.9%).
* Management moderated its FY27 AUM growth guidance to ~15-17% from ~18% earlier, factoring in weak monsoons and uncertainty arising from the West Asia conflict. Despite healthy demand over the past two quarters, SHFL remains cautious in drought-affected states such as Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Telangana, where it has a sizeable portfolio.
* SHFL indicated that credit costs could rise temporarily by 30-40bp over the next one or two quarters due to seasonal stress in affected geographies, but they are still expected to remain below ~2.3% for FY27. Elevated stress is mainly attributable to deficient rainfall and seasonal pressures in select regions, with no evidence of widespread portfolio deterioration. Lower agricultural output could weigh on rural incomes, consumption, and borrower cash flows in the coming quarters. The asset quality outlook for the company remains cautious amid these near-term headwinds.
* We tweak our FY27/FY28 EPS estimates to factor in higher credit costs, offset by higher NIM and lower opex. We expect SHFL to deliver a CAGR of ~18%/~31% in AUM/PAT over FY26-28E, along with RoA/RoE of ~4.1%/ 13.7% by FY28. We reiterate our BUY rating with a TP of INR1,155 (premised on 2x Sep’28E BVPS)
 AUM rises ~17% YoY; disbursement growth healthy 
* Disbursements grew 25% YoY to INR541b in 2QFY27. AUM stood at INR3.29t (slightly higher than our estimates) and grew ~17% YoY/4.9% QoQ. AUM growth was strong across CV, PV, gold loans and personal loans, while growth in CE, farm equipment, and 2W remained relatively weak during the quarter.
* Management shared that the strong disbursement growth in MSME was supported by expansion beyond its traditional southern and western markets to a pan-India presence following the merger. The company expects MSME lending to outpace growth in other segments. We anticipate disbursement/AUM growth of 19%/17% in FY27.
 Highlights from the management commentary 
* Management shared that moisture stress has affected rice, soybean, maize, cotton, and pulses, while fertilizer shortages amid West Asia-related disruptions could further pressure food supply.
* The company highlighted that weak monsoons are weighing on rural consumption, particularly entry-level two-wheelers and cars, discretionary FMCG, and consumer appliances. However, diversification into non-farm and allied activities, greater irrigation coverage, and lower rainfall dependence have improved rural resilience.
* SHFL delivered a mixed quarter, with PPoP beating estimates on the back of higher NIM and lower opex, while earnings were in line owing to higher credit costs. AUM growth at 17% YoY was stronger than our estimate; however, credit costs increased amid higher slippages and write-offs, primarily reflecting drought-like conditions across multiple states in India. Hence, management raised its FY27 credit cost guidance and lowered its AUM growth outlook.
* The stock is currently trading at 1.5x FY28E P/BV. We expect SHFL to deliver a CAGR of ~18%/~31% in AUM/PAT over FY26-28E, along with an RoA/RoE of ~4.1%/13.7% in FY28. We reiterate our BUY rating with a TP of INR1,155 (premised on 2x Sep’28E BVPS).

docs.title: Upgrade to Buy BSE Ltd For Target Rs.4,000 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
* BSE’s F&O notional ADTO surged 85% in Oct’26MTD vs. the post-CAS reset in Aug’26 (-34% MoM). With the partial CAS reversal effective 7-Dec-26, the recovery has a regulatory catalyst beyond the current volatility-led spike. We expect FY27 ADTO of INR216t (+16% YoY), with upside potential if the recovery sustains.
* While BSE has achieved a 30%+ market share in premium turnover, further marketshare expansion remains possible. The premium-to-notional ratio has already climbed to ~14bp from 6–7bp in 2023–24, against 20bp+ for NSE. Further convergence, driven by institutional participation and longer-dated contracts, can deliver meaningful earnings upside over and above volume growth.
* Cash market share has improved from ~7% to ~9%, while NSE’s listing and the opening of its lock-in in Mar’27 offer a further catalyst for turnover. Improving smart-order routing and platform participation strengthen the case for a sustained step-up in cash-market activity with the FY26-28 ADTO CAGR expected at 30%.
* Star MF has scaled notably from 12m quarterly transactions in 1QFY20 to 245m in 2QFY27, generating INR800m+ in quarterly revenue. Co-location already contributes INR450-480m per quarter, with further capacity and pricing headroom. These businesses broaden BSE’s earnings drivers beyond trading activity alone.
* Every incremental rupee of revenue has the potential to deliver healthy profit growth. BSE’s EBITDA margin expanded to 65%+ in FY26 from 9% in FY21, demonstrating the scalability of its model. With margins expected to reach 70%, we forecast a ~27% FY26- 28 PAT CAGR on a 23% revenue CAGR. The variable nature of regulatory costs (55% of opex) provides a degree of insulation against volume slowdowns.
* We raise our revenue and PAT estimates by 8%/10% and 10%/12%, respectively, for FY27/FY28, supported by the strong volume run-rate, the likely benefit of the CAS reversal and the benefit of NSE listing on cash volumes. A sustained volume recovery combined with an improving premium-to-notional (P/N) ratio could drive a further ~20% increase in FY28E PAT. We upgrade the stock to BUY with a TP of INR4,000 (based on 40x FY28E P/E).
 Volume reset over; growth path looks better ahead! 
* Since BSE relaunched derivatives in 2023, the impact of most regulatory changes, including F&O 2.0 and the change in weekly expiry day, has been transient. BSE achieved ~50% market share in index options notional turnover within three years of the relaunch, while volumes continued to show strong momentum.
* However, the recent regulatory changes—stricter lending norms for proprietary traders (effective Jul’26) and CAS implementation (Aug’26)—led to a reset in the volume base, with BSE’s notional F&O ADTO falling 35% in Aug’26 compared with the Apr-Jul’26 average.
* Following the base reset in Aug’26, Sep’26 witnessed a modest recovery, with ADTO growing 6% MoM. However, aided by volatile markets, Oct’26 has seen a significant spurt in volumes, with ADTO up 49% MoM as of 20th Oct’26.
* Moreover, SEBI’s recent circular has partially reversed the CAS reforms, restoring last-30-minute VWAP settlement for index derivatives from 7th Dec’26 and addressing the expiry-day volatility that hit traders and HFTs in Aug’26.
* While the Oct’26 data has shown a strong recovery in volumes driven by market volatility, we believe that the CAS reversal would lead to volume normalization.
* Prop traders account for 48.9% of BSE derivatives turnover, down from 58.4% in Apr’25, reflecting diversification of participant mix and insulating BSE from the impact due to stricter lending norms, to a certain extent.
* BSE’s notional ADTO for YTDFY27 stands at INR 213t, and we expect FY27 ADTO to be INR 216t, aided by volume normalization following Dec’26. Heightened volatility during that period may lead to a further upgrade to our volume estimates
* While CAS weighed on volumes in Aug’26, Sep’26 witnessed a recovery, and Oct’26 volumes have surged, supported by market volatility. With the partial reversal of CAS effective from Dec’26, derivatives activity should normalize faster, supporting top-line growth and, in turn, margin expansion through operating leverage.
* We expect BSE to witness a strong recovery in volume growth, aided by rising member participation an improving P/N ratio. An improved growth trajectory in the cash segment, robust demand for co-location, and the strong positioning of the Star MF platform will also contribute to the company’s performance.
* We raise our revenue and PAT estimates by 8%/10% and 10%/12%, respectively, for FY27/FY28, supported by the strong volume run-rate, the likely benefit of the CAS reversal and the benefit of NSE listing on cash volumes. A sustained volume recovery combined with an improving premium-to-notional (P/N) ratio could drive a further ~20% increase in FY28E PAT. We upgrade the stock to BUY with a TP of INR4,000 (based on 40x FY28E P/E).

docs.title: Buy Adani Ports & SEZ Ltd For Target Rs.2,130 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
Strong 2Q volume recovery; expansion to drive growth 
* All-India major port volumes increased 10% YoY in 2QFY27 and 8.1% in FY27’YTD, led by strong growth in container (+8%), POL (+7%) and coal (+7%) volume. Non-major port volumes inched up 1% YoY due to a 7% decline in coal volume. POL (petroleum, oil and lubricants) volume, with a cargo share of 26%, remained flat, while container cargo grew ~6%. APSEZ outperformed the industry, handling ~142mt of cargo in 2Q, up 15% YoY. Growth in 1H was driven by strong traction in dry cargo and containers, primarily led by NQXT, along with a recovery in container volumes following the slowdown caused by port disruption amid the Middle East crisis. On a YTD basis, APSEZ’s cargo volumes rose 15% YoY to 280mt, supported by healthy growth in container (+15%) and dry bulk (+15%) volume.
* In line with its vision of handling 1b tons of cargo by 2030, the company has recently received a letter of award (LoA) for the development and operation of two dry bulk berths at Paradip Port, Odisha. The project entails a capacity of 18mt and a concession period of 30 years, taking the company’s total capacity to 671mt. The terminal will strengthen its presence in eastern India and enhance its ability to handle coal, limestone and other dry bulk commodities.
* The recent expansion of Colombo Port’s capacity from 24mt to 48mt will enhance its ability to handle higher cargo volumes and accommodate larger vessels. APSEZ handled ~7mt of cargo at the port in 1QFY27 against the existing capacity of 24mt per annum. The expanded capacity provides significant headroom for volume growth, strengthening the port’s ability to capture rising transshipment demand and support APSEZ’s long-term cargo growth.
* With strong volume recovery in 2QFY27, particularly in dry cargo and containers, and improving earnings visibility, APSEZ remains well positioned to sustain its growth trajectory despite ongoing geopolitical uncertainties. Continued expansion of port capacity, marine services, and integrated end-toend logistics should support long-term growth. These initiatives reinforce APSEZ’s ambition to become India’s largest integrated transport utility by 2031, with Logistics and Marine emerging as key growth engines alongside its core port business. We reiterate our BUY rating with a TP of INR2,130, based on 17x FY28E EV/EBITDA.
 Scale leadership and rising market share underpin long-term growth outlook 
* APSEZ operates the largest private port network in India, with 15 ports and terminals across the West, South, and East coasts. The network offers a total capacity of 671mmt. It also operates four international ports in Israel, Sri Lanka, Tanzania, and Australia.
* The company has commissioned the Haldia bulk terminal in Mar’26, with a capacity of ~4mtpa and a draft of 8.5m, supported by a dedicated rail line and integrated conveyor system.
* APSEZ’s domestic market share stood at 27.6% as of Jun’26. Management highlighted that its domestic port volume growth over the past decade has been more than twice the industry growth rate.
* The container market share has also expanded steadily to 45.5% from 36% during Mar’20-Mar’26. Key capacity expansions, such as the automated Colombo West International Terminal and new berths at Dhamra, along with the rapid ramp-up of Vizhinjam, are strengthening APSEZ’s growth pipeline.
* Going forward, management retains its target of achieving 850mmt of domestic and 150mmt of international cargo volumes by 2030, with deeper integration into DFC-linked hinterland corridors and industrial clusters driving long-term growth.
* With strong cash flows, a healthy cash balance of INR124b, and a net debt-toEBITDA ratio of 1.9x, APSEZ is well-positioned for further expansion. Capacity enhancements at key ports, ongoing infrastructure projects, and global port acquisitions provide visibility for stable growth in FY27 and beyond.
* APSEZ’s diversified cargo mix, port location and ongoing infrastructure investments are expected to support its volume growth. We anticipate APSEZ to report 14% growth in cargo volumes over FY26-28. This growth is likely to drive a CAGR of 17%/18%/21% in revenue/EBITDA/PAT over FY26-28E. We reiterate our BUY rating on the stock with a TP of INR2,130 (premised on 17x FY28E EV/EBITDA).

docs.title: Buy Coforge Ltd For Target Rs.2,370 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
A quarter for integration Margin push encouraging as benefits from AI continue 
? COFORGE reported 2QFY27 organic revenue growth of 3.8% QoQ in CC terms, above our estimate of 3.5% QoQ CC. The company reported an order intake of USD1,040m (up 102.3% YoY) with eight large deal wins. Consolidated EBIT margin stood at 16%, in line with our estimate.
? Consolidated adjusted PAT stood at INR6.3b (up 12.5% QoQ/67.8% YoY), in line with our estimate.
? 1HFY27 revenue/EBIT/adj. PAT grew 52.1%/78.8%/59.8% YoY. In 2HFY27, we expect revenue/EBIT/adj. PAT growth of 51.5%/58.1%/47.6% YoY in INR terms. We value COFORGE at 32x FY28E EPS with a TP of INR2,370, implying a 25% potential upside. We reiterate our BUY rating on the stock.
 Our view: Strong order book supports growth acceleration in 2H 
* Deal momentum remains strong, supporting growth visibility: Coforge reported a record quarterly order intake of USD1.04b, up 51% QoQ and 102% YoY, with eight large deal wins. The next 12-month executable order book rose 45% YoY to a record USD2.4b. With eight or more large deal wins targeted in 3QFY27, deal momentum is expected to support growth visibility. Most large deals are proactively sourced and solution-led, limiting direct pricing competition.
* Encora integration nearing completion; growth expected to accelerate in 2HFY27: YoY organic growth has decelerated over the past two quarters, partly reflecting the Encora integration, with Encora's revenue remaining broadly flat QoQ at USD147-148m in 2QFY27. With integration largely complete, Encora's growth is expected to converge with Coforge's from 3QFY27. Encora's margin expansion is also ahead of the acquisition plan, while a strong deal pipeline, including the largest deal currently being pursued with an Encora client and expected to close in 3Q or 4Q, provides further growth opportunities.
* Margin trajectory improving, with further expansion levers: Margin gains have so far been supported by G&A efficiency, with G&A growing only 15.6% YoY against revenue and sales and marketing growth of ~52% YoY. Further improvement is expected from AI-led efficiency and high utilization, currently at 82.4% vs. ~86% for peers. Gross margin expansion is expected to become more visible from 4QFY27. We expect consolidated EBIT margins at 16% in FY27E and build in 40bp improvement in FY28E. The margin upgrade, alongside continued investment in sales and solutioning, supports the view that profitability gains are not being pursued at the expense of growth.
* Organic growth led by BFSI and government; healthcare and high-tech decline: Organic QoQ CC revenue growth was led by government outside India (+20.8% QoQ), BFSI (+8.3%), insurance (+3.6%), emerging verticals (+2.3%), and travel, transportation and hospitality (+1.8%). Healthcare and high-tech declined 6.4%. Organic growth led by BFSI and government; healthcare and high-tech decline: Organic QoQ CC revenue growth was led by government outside India (+20.8% QoQ), BFSI (+8.3%), insurance (+3.6%), emerging verticals (+2.3%), and travel, transportation and hospitality (+1.8%). Healthcare and high-tech declined 6.4%.
* Cash conversion on track despite temporary collection delays: FCF-to-PAT conversion stood at 89% in 2Q, with 100% conversion targeted for FY27. OCFto-EBITDA (~42%) conversion has been affected by the transfer of contracts from US entities to India as part of Encora’s legal entity rationalization and tax structuring, resulting in temporary delays in invoicing and collections.
* We expect COFORGE to be the growth leader within our coverage universe, and we reiterate it as our top pick. Strong deal wins, continued execution, improving cash conversion, and EBIT margin guidance upgrade, along with further expansion in FY28, provide confidence in the medium-term growth outlook.
* We keep our estimates unchanged and raise our target multiple to 32x FY28E EPS (earlier 29x), arriving at a TP of INR2,370, implying 25% upside. The higher multiple reflects improved visibility from strong deal wins and structurally higher margins. We reiterate our BUY rating on the stock

docs.title: Buy SBI Funds Management Ltd For Target Rs.590 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
EBITDA in line; other income drives PAT beat 
* SBI Funds Management’s (SBIFUNDS) operating revenue grew 9% YoY/4% QoQ to ~INR11.9b (in line). Yields came in at 36.4bp in 2QFY27 vs 36.5bp in 2QFY26 and 36.7bp in 1QFY27. For 1HFY27, operating revenue grew 12% YoY.
* Total opex stood at INR2.8b (19% higher than est.), growing 22% YoY/22% QoQ. EBITDA came in at INR9.1b (in line), rising 5% YoY. EBITDA margin stood at 76.5% vs 79.1% in 2QFY26 and 80.1% in 1QFY27.
* Beat on other income resulted in 7% PAT beat, which stood at INR7b, declining 6% YoY and 20% QoQ. For 1HFY27, PAT declined 1% YoY. PAT margin stood at 58.8% vs 68.1% in 2QFY26 and 76.4% in 1QFY27.
* The marginal decline in blended yields was attributed to a change in asset mix rather than broad-based pressure on product yields. On the expense front, employee expenses are expected to remain at the 2Q run rate going forward.
* We have broadly kept our estimates intact considering the in line operating performance in 2QFY27. We reiterate our BUY rating on the stock with a TP of INR590, based on a valuation of 38x FY28E core P/E.
 MF AUM continues to grow with industry leading market share of 15% 
* Overall MF QAAUM grew 9% YoY/4% QoQ to INR13.1t, driven by 12%/18%/10%/22% YoY growth in equity (incl. hybrid)/liquid/ETF/other QAAUM, while debt QAAUM declined 20% YoY.
* Overall, average AUM declined 6% YoY due to a decline in PMS & advisory AUM to INR26.5t in 2QFY27, with the asset mix comprising equity at 23%, debt at 6%, liquid at 6%, passives at 16%, and AIF/PMS assets at 50%.
* PMS & advisory QAAUM declined 17% YoY to ~INR13.3t (INR16.1t in 2QFY26) due to the reallocation of a large institutional mandate; however, the impact on revenue is not material.
* AIF QAAUM increased 25% YoY to INR74b. Yields on the non-mutual fund business are approximately 35–40bp, excluding the advisory component.
* Passive QAAUM stood at INR4.15t as of Sep’26, growing 11% YoY, indicating a market share of 27.4%. SIF QAAUM stood at INR44b, indicating a market share of 16.2% vs INR35b in 1QFY27.
* Monthly SIP flows improved 3% YoY to INR39b for Sep’26, with SIP AUM at INR2.1t (+15% YoY), indicating a market share of 12.3%. 3.6m fresh SIPs were added during the quarter, taking the live SIP count to 16.2m.
* In terms of channel mix, the direct channel continued to dominate the overall asset sourcing mix with a 57% share, followed by banks at 24%, with SBI contributing 21%, MFDs 11%, and national distributors 11%.
* In terms of equity MAAUM, the distribution mix for MFDs/national distributors/direct/SBI/other banks stood at 20%/13%/27%/35%/5%.
* Unique customers stood at 18.5m as of Sep’26, rising 10% YoY. Total live folios stood at 22.7m, rising 12% YoY during the same period.
* Five products were launched in 2QFY27, including one SIF. The pipeline across mutual funds, AIFs, PMS, and SIFs provides opportunities to widen the product offering.
* Opex, as a percentage of QAAUM, stood at 8.3bp in 2QFY27 vs. 7.4bp in 2QFY26 (est. 7.3bp).
* Employee costs at ~INR1.3b (22% higher than est.) rose 21% YoY/25% QoQ.
* Other expenses at ~INR1.4b (15% higher than est.) rose 22% YoY/18% QoQ.
* Overall expenses increased due to one-off technology infrastructure spending and the appointment of a new AIF business head.
* Other income came in at INR447m vs INR1b in 2QFY26 and our expectation of negative INR250m.
* The mutual fund business remains strong, supported by continued growth in AUM, resilient SIP flows, and a robust SBI-backed distribution network. Continued improvement in flows and yields remains key earnings drivers. PMS & advisory business earnings remain unaffected by the reallocation of a large mandate, while AIF and SIF AUM continue to rise. Increased investments in technology are expected to enhance productivity.
* We have broadly kept our estimates intact, considering the in line operating performance in 2QFY27. We reiterate our BUY rating on the stock with a TP of INR590, based on a valuation of 38x FY28E core P/E.

docs.title: Buy Infosys Ltd For Target Rs. 1,300 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
FY27 growth outlook softens Daimler deal to weigh on exit-growth; margins hold up despite pricing pressure 
* Infosys (INFO) reported 2QFY27 revenue of USD5.1b, up 1.2% QoQ. In CC, it was up 1.2% QoQ, below our estimate of 1.8% QoQ. Adj. EBIT margin stood at 21%, in line with our estimate of 21.1%. Adj. EBIT rose 1.6% QoQ/10.4% YoY to INR103b (est. INR104b). Adj. PAT came in at INR78b, up 0.6% QoQ/ 6.2% YoY, below our estimate of INR81b.
* FY27 revenue growth guidance was lowered to 1-2% YoY in CC (vs. 1.5-3.0% earlier) and organic growth guidance was reduced to -0.5% to 0.5% (vs. - 0.2% to 1.3% earlier). Adj. EBIT margin guidance was maintained in the 20- 22% range. Large deal TCV stood at USD5.2b, up 44.4% QoQ/67.7% YoY. The book-to-bill ratio was 1.0x.
* For 1HFY27, revenue/adj. EBIT/adj. PAT grew 12.3%/12.9%/9.1% YoY in INR terms. In 2HFY27, we expect INFO’s revenue/adj. EBIT to grow 5.9%/4.6% YoY and adj. PAT to decline 0.6% YoY. We value INFO at 16x FY28E EPS with a TP of INR1,300, implying a 13% upside potential. Retain BUY.
 Our view: Peer underperformance likely to continue 
* Guidance cut points to weaker growth; underperformance vs. peers likely to continue: A confluence of factors such as weaker volumes, lower-thanexpected price increases, offshoring and the decision to walk away from a large European manufacturing deal has weighed on growth. INFO has cut its FY27 revenue growth guidance to 1-2% YoY CC from 1.5-3.0%, while organic growth guidance was reduced to -0.5% to 0.5% from -0.2% to 1.3%. We expect QoQ revenue decline in the next two quarters due to seasonality.
* The shift toward offshore delivery and the deal exit are expected to have a 1.8-2.0% impact on FY27 growth. We estimate revenue growth of 1.1%/1.9% YoY CC in FY27/FY28, and expect INFO to grow slower than HCLT, TCS and TECHM in both years, based on our estimates.
* Daimler deal creates 4Q exit uncertainty and will weigh on FY28 growth as well: The impact of exiting the Daimler deal is expected to be largely felt in 4Q, creating uncertainty around the exit growth rate in FY28. While the new mega deal should support growth in FY28, the timing and pace of ramp-up remain key monitorables. The CEO transition is a short-term overhang amid a weak growth environment and continued pricing pressure.
* Margins holding up but pricing pressure apparent; expect range-bound performance in the medium term: INFO maintained its EBIT margin guidance of 20-22%. However, competitive intensity has prevented the expected price increases, while wage hikes, acquisition amortization and softer seasonality are likely to weigh on margins in 2H. We estimate EBIT margins of 21% for FY27/FY28 both and expect margins to remain rangebound in the medium term.
* Deal wins a silver lining: Large deal TCV stood at USD5.2b, with 62% net new deals, including a USD2b+ mega deal expected to contribute over 1% to FY28 growth. AI revenue increased to 10.5% of revenue (8.2% in 1QFY27), up 29% QoQ. While deal wins and AI revenue provide some support, the key monitorable is whether these translate into better overall revenue growth.
* We trim our FY27/FY28 EPS estimates by ~1.5%/2.0% to factor in lower FY27 organic growth guidance and continued pricing pressure from AI-led productivity deflation. While AI revenue continues to scale up, we believe productivity pass-through on the existing book of business will remain a nearterm headwind. Execution on deal conversion and pricing remains a key monitorable. We value INFO at 16x FY28E EPS and arrive at a TP of INR1,300, implying ~13% upside. Reiterate BUY.

docs.title: Buy Jindal Steel Ltd For Target Rs.1,270 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
Operating performance marginally better than estimates; outlook remains strong 
* Jindal Steel’s (JINDALST) revenue stood at INR167b (+43% YoY and +8% QoQ; vs our est. of INR156b), driven by higher volume and NSR during 2QFY27.
* Adj. EBITDA stood at INR25.7b (+38% YoY and -3% QoQ) against our est. of INR22.9b during the quarter. This translates to EBITDA/t of INR10,800 vs our estimate of INR9,800/t in 2QFY27.
* The sequential decline in EBITDA was led by cost escalation due to a surge in coking coal costs by ~USD12-14/t QoQ in 2QFY27, which was broadly in line with earlier management guidance.
* APAT for the quarter stood at INR7.7b (+79% YoY and -8% QoQ), against our estimate of INR8.5b in 2QFY27 on account of higher tax outgo.
* Production for 2QFY27 stood at 2.4mt (+20% YoY; flat QoQ) despite seasonally weak quarter. Sales volume stood at 2.38MT (+27% YoY and +7% QoQ), supported by inventory liquidation. The share of exports stood at 8% in 2QFY27, compared to 9% in 1QFY27.
* NSR rose 12% YoY and 1% QoQ to INR70,000/t on account of a higher share of flats in the overall sales mix and lower TMT sales within longs.
* The consolidated net debt stood at INR148b as of Sep’26, compared to INR159b in Jun’26. Net Debt/EBITDA improved to 1.51x in 2QFY27 against 1.71x in 1QFY27.
 Key highlights from the management commentary 
* Management reiterated its FY27 production volume target of ~11mt, with ~6mt target in 2H at run rate of ~0.96mt per month. The product mix target stands at 65% flats and 35% long products, while the current mix stands at ~60:40.
* VAP mix stood at 57% during 2QFY27. Management indicated that the mix exceeds 65%, with the shift from lower-priced TMT toward higher-priced flat products and other realizations-enhancing categories.
* Exports are currently running at ~100kt per month, primarily comprising HRC and plates, alongside some rails and structural steel. Management expects further export opportunities from improved access to European markets, although EU quota restrictions and CBAM remain key considerations.
* HRC and TMT spot prices have reached ~INR60,000/t, compared with lower levels during the earlier part of 2QFY27. HRC prices strengthened toward Aug-Sept, while TMT prices recovered from monsoon-related weakness. The company expects realizations to improve further in 3QFY27 and 4QFY27, supported by seasonal demand recovery and stronger steel prices.
* Management expects coal price to increase ~USD20-25/t in 3QFY27, although prices have recently stabilized. The potential resumption of Russian coal supplies through the Black Sea could ease global coking coal prices in Dec’26-Jan’27, subject to geopolitical developments.
* JINDALST reported healthy earnings in 2QFY27 on account of higher volumes and NSR despite the seasonally weak quarter. Costs escalated during the quarter, mainly over higher raw material, power & fuel, and freight costs. Management expects further cost inflation in the coming quarters, which could largely offset the benefits of elevated steel price and superior VAP share.
* We remain positive on JINDALST’s long-term outlook, where the recent increase in its crude steel capacity to 15.6mtpa provides significant headroom for earnings growth. Further, the prevailing safeguard duty is expected to keep domestic steel prices steady, supporting margins against input cost volatility.
* A large proportion of capex has already been incurred, and the rest would be funded through internal accruals, keeping net debt/EBITDA below the threshold level of 1.5x. Net debt stood at INR147b in 2QFY27, translating into a net debt/EBITDA of 1.5x.
* At CMP, the stock trades at 6.7x EV/EBITDA on FY28E. We largely maintain our estimates for FY28 and reiterate our BUY rating with a TP of INR1,270, based on 8x EV/EBITDA on the FY28E.
